events.title: Alexander Graham Bell Granted Telephone Patent
events.description: The U.S. Patent Office issued Patent No. 174,465 to Alexander Graham Bell for his invention of the telephone, covering the method of transmitting speech by telegraphic means.
events.significance: The patent protected one of the most transformative inventions in history, launching modern telecommunications and the Bell Telephone Company.

events.title: Germany Remilitarizes the Rhineland
events.description: Adolf Hitler ordered German troops into the demilitarized Rhineland, violating the Treaty of Versailles and the Locarno Treaties. France and Britain did not respond with military action.
events.significance: The lack of response emboldened Hitler and showed the weakness of appeasement, a key step on the road to World War II.

events.title: Bloody Sunday in Selma
events.description: About 600 civil rights marchers led by John Lewis and Hosea Williams were attacked by state troopers and local police as they crossed the Edmund Pettus Bridge in Selma, Alabama, en route to Montgomery.
events.significance: Televised images of the violence shocked the nation, building support for the Voting Rights Act of 1965 and advancing the American civil rights movement.

events.title: Capture of the Ludendorff Bridge at Remagen
events.description: U.S. 9th Armored Division forces captured the Ludendorff Bridge over the Rhine at Remagen, Germany, largely intact, allowing Allied troops to cross the river.
events.significance: The unexpected crossing gave the Allies a foothold east of the Rhine and hastened the collapse of Nazi Germany in World War II.

events.title: Birth of Maurice Ravel
events.description: French composer Maurice Ravel was born in Ciboure, France. He became known for works such as Boléro, Pavane for a Dead Princess, and his orchestration of Pictures at an Exhibition.
events.significance: Ravel became one of the most influential composers of the early 20th century, noted for his orchestral mastery and refined impressionist style.
